facts.subject: HASS / History
facts.fact: Australia became a nation on 1 January 1901 when the six colonies federated.
facts.evidence: Australia becomes a nation on 1 January 1901 when the six colonies federate.

facts.subject: HASS / History
facts.fact: Edmund Barton was sworn in as Australia's first Prime Minister in 1901.
facts.evidence: Edmund Barton is sworn in as Australia’s first Prime Minister.

facts.subject: HASS / History
facts.fact: The first Parliament of the Commonwealth of Australia opened in Melbourne on 9 May 1901.
facts.evidence: The members of the Australian Parliament assemble for the first time in Melbourne on 9 May 1901.

facts.subject: HASS / History
facts.fact: The first Commonwealth Parliament comprised 111 members: 36 senators and 75 members of the House of Representatives.
facts.evidence: the Parliament comprises 111 members (36 senators and 75 members of the House of Representatives).

facts.subject: HASS / History
facts.fact: The Canberra–Yass district was chosen as the site of Australia's new national capital in 1908.

facts.subject: Geography
facts.fact: Australia is the world's sixth largest country by area.
facts.evidence: Australia is the world's sixth largest country, after Russia, Canada, China, the USA, and Brazil.

facts.subject: Curriculum
facts.fact: The F–10 Australian Curriculum identifies 8 learning areas.
facts.evidence: The F–10 Australian Curriculum identifies and organises ... 8 learning areas.

facts.subject: Mathematics
facts.fact: Australian Curriculum Mathematics is organised into 6 strands: Number, Algebra, Measurement, Space, Statistics and Probability.
facts.evidence: Content is organised under 6 interrelated strands: Number, Algebra, Measurement, Space, Statistics and Probability.

facts.subject: English
facts.fact: Australian Curriculum English is organised into 3 interrelated strands: Language, Literature and Literacy.
facts.evidence: Content is organised under 3 interrelated strands: Language, Literature, Literacy.

facts.subject: Science
facts.fact: Australian Curriculum Science is organised into 3 interrelated strands: Science understanding, Science as a human endeavour, and Science inquiry.
facts.evidence: Content is organised under 3 interrelated strands: Science understanding, Science as a human endeavour, Science inquiry.

facts.subject: HASS
facts.fact: Australian Curriculum Humanities and Social Sciences Foundation to Year 10 comprises 5 subjects.
facts.evidence: The Australian Curriculum: Humanities and Social Sciences Foundation to Year 10 comprises 5 subjects.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: In Year 9 History, students study Making and transforming the Australian nation (1759–1914) and the First World War.
facts.canonicalAnswer: Making and transforming the Australian nation; First World War
facts.evidence: Making and transforming the Australian nation (1759–1914) and the First World War in Year 9.

facts.subject: History
facts.fact: In Year 10 History, students study the Second World War and Building modern Australia (1945–present).
facts.canonicalAnswer: Second World War; Building modern Australia
facts.evidence: the Second World War and Building modern Australia (1945 – present) in Year 10.

facts.subject: HASS
facts.fact: Civics and Citizenship is introduced in HASS from Year 3, and Economics and Business from Year 5.
facts.evidence: Civics and Citizenship from Year 3, and Economics and Business from Year 5.

facts.subject: Science
facts.fact: Years 3 and 4 STEM curriculum links include scientific concepts such as heat, soils, rocks and minerals, the water cycle, forces, ecosystems, lifecycles and material properties.
facts.evidence: They explore various scientific concepts, such as heat ... soils, rocks and minerals ... water cycle ... forces ... ecosystems ... lifecycles ... material properties.

questions.question: On what date did Australia become a nation through Federation?
questions.explanation: The six Australian colonies federated and the Commonwealth of Australia came into existence on 1 January 1901.

questions.question: Who was Australia's first Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Edmund Barton was sworn in as Australia's first Prime Minister in 1901.

questions.question: When did the first Commonwealth Parliament of Australia open?
questions.explanation: The first Commonwealth Parliament opened in Melbourne on 9 May 1901.

questions.question: How many members were in Australia's first Commonwealth Parliament?
questions.explanation: It comprised 111 members: 36 senators and 75 House of Representatives members.

questions.question: By area, where does Australia rank among the world's largest countries?
questions.explanation: Geoscience Australia describes Australia as the world's sixth largest country.

questions.question: Which Australian state or territory has the largest total area?
questions.explanation: Western Australia has the largest total area in Geoscience Australia's state and territory table.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain on the Australian mainland?
questions.explanation: Mount Kosciuszko is the highest mountain on the Australian mainland.

questions.question: How high is Mount Kosciuszko according to Geoscience Australia?
questions.explanation: Mount Kosciuszko is listed at 2,228 metres above sea level.

questions.question: What is Australia's average elevation?
questions.explanation: Geoscience Australia states Australia's average elevation is only about 330 metres.

questions.question: Lake Eyre is listed at 15 metres below sea level.
questions.explanation: Geoscience Australia lists Lake Eyre at 15 metres below sea level.

questions.question: What was Australia's estimated resident population at 31 December 2025?
questions.explanation: ABS reported 27,801,023 people at 31 December 2025.

questions.question: Which state or territory had Australia's fastest annual population growth rate at 31 December 2025?
questions.explanation: ABS reported Western Australia had the fastest growth rate, at 2.2%.

questions.question: When was Australian Curriculum Version 9.0 endorsed?
questions.explanation: Australian Curriculum's version history lists Version 9.0 as 10 May 2022.

questions.question: How many learning areas are identified in the F–10 Australian Curriculum?
questions.explanation: The F–10 Australian Curriculum identifies 8 learning areas.

questions.question: Which of these are strands in Australian Curriculum Mathematics?
questions.explanation: Mathematics has six strands including Number, Space and Statistics. Literature belongs to English.

questions.question: Which set lists the three strands of Australian Curriculum English?
questions.explanation: English is organised into Language, Literature and Literacy.

questions.question: Which is one of the three strands of Australian Curriculum Science?
questions.explanation: Science inquiry is one of the three Science strands.

questions.question: Australian Curriculum Humanities and Social Sciences Foundation to Year 10 comprises five subjects.
questions.explanation: The Australian Curriculum states that HASS Foundation to Year 10 comprises five subjects.

questions.question: Which topics are required in Year 9 Australian Curriculum History?
options: Making and transforming the Australian nation (1759–1914)
questions.correctAnswer: Making and transforming the Australian nation (1759–1914); The First World War
questions.explanation: Year 9 includes Making and transforming the Australian nation and the First World War.

questions.question: Which topics are required in Year 10 Australian Curriculum History?
questions.correctAnswer: The Second World War; Building modern Australia (1945–present)
questions.explanation: Year 10 includes the Second World War and Building modern Australia.

questions.question: From which year is Civics and Citizenship introduced in F–6 HASS?
questions.explanation: Civics and Citizenship is introduced from Year 3.

questions.question: From which year is Economics and Business introduced in F–6 HASS?
questions.explanation: Economics and Business is introduced from Year 5.

questions.question: What total area does Geoscience Australia list for Australia?
questions.explanation: Geoscience Australia lists Australia's total area as 7,688,287 square kilometres.

questions.question: What is Victoria's highest mountain?
questions.explanation: Geoscience Australia lists Mount Bogong as Victoria's highest mountain.

questions.question: What is Tasmania's highest mountain?
questions.explanation: Geoscience Australia lists Mount Ossa as Tasmania's highest mountain.

questions.question: What is the highest mountain in the Australian Capital Territory?
questions.explanation: Geoscience Australia lists Bimberi Peak as the ACT's highest mountain.

questions.question: In what year was the Canberra–Yass district chosen as the site of Australia's national capital?
questions.explanation: The Canberra–Yass district was chosen as the site of the new national capital in 1908.

questions.question: In what year was land ceded to the Commonwealth to form the Australian Capital Territory?
questions.explanation: An area was ceded to the Commonwealth in 1911, forming the Australian Capital Territory.

questions.question: Which of these scientific concepts appear in the Australian Curriculum STEM connections for Years 3 and 4?
questions.explanation: The Years 3 and 4 STEM links include forces, the water cycle and ecosystems among the listed scientific concepts.
